plan_a_advantages: More intense workouts (intervals, hills) directly targeting trail running speed and power.
Longer runs contribute to greater overall endurance and resilience.
Incorporates cross-training for maintaining fitness without excessive impact.
plan_b_advantages: Shorter, less demanding workouts may be better suited for a runner who is new to structured training or recovering from injury.
Focus on consistency and building a solid aerobic base is a valuable foundation for any runner.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted and demanding workouts designed to build speed and strength specific to trail running. While Plan B includes tempo and hill work, Plan A’s inclusion of interval sessions and a longer, dedicated hill workout provides a greater stimulus for improving running economy and power – crucial for trail speed. Furthermore, Plan A’s longer runs and cross-training contribute to overall endurance and resilience, which are vital for tackling the varied terrain of trail races. Plan B’s shorter sessions and focus on consistency, while beneficial, don’t provide the same level of intensity needed for significant performance gains.
